claim: Blindness affects millions of people around the world, with an estimated 43.3 million people blind as per 2020.
source: Globally, as per 2020, an estimated 43.3 million people were blind (Bourne et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bourne et al., 2021.

claim: Visual prosthetics may provide a promising solution for some cases of blindness.
source: For some cases of blindness, visual prosthetics may provide a promising solution.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fernandez, 2018; Bloch et al., 2019; Nowik et al., 2020 in the surrounding context.

claim: Visual prosthetic devices aim to restore a rudimentary form of vision by interacting with the visual system using electrical stimulation.
source: These devices aim to restore a rudimentary form of vision by interacting with the visual system using electrical stimulation (Fernandez, 2018; Bloch et al., 2019; Nowik et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The artificially induced visual percepts consist of patterns of localized light flashes called 'phosphenes' with limited resolution.
source: The artificially induced visual percepts consist of patterns of localized light flashes ('phosphenes') with a limited resolution.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge in the field of visual prosthetics.

claim: Scene-processing is required to condense complex visual information from the surroundings into an intelligible pattern of phosphenes to achieve a functional level of vision.
source: To achieve a functional level of vision, scene-processing is required to condense complex visual information from the surroundings in an intelligible pattern of phosphenes (de Ruyter van Steveninck et al., 2022a; Lozano et al., 2020; Normann et al., 2009; Sanchez-Garcia et al., 2020; Troyk, 2017; Granley et al., 2022a; Han et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to relevant studies.

claim: Early attempts by Brindley and Lewin, and Dobelle successfully reported the ability to reliably induce the perception of phosphenes via electrical stimulation of the cortical surface.
source: Early attempts by Brindley and Lewin, and Dobelle successfully reported the ability to reliably induce the perception of phosphenes (described as localized round flashes of light) via electrical stimulation of the cortical surface (Brindley and Lewin, 1968; Dobelle and Mladejovsky, 1974).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to historical studies.

claim: Recent preclinical studies demonstrate promising results concerning the safety and efficacy of long-term stimulation in the primary visual cortex.
source: More recent preclinical studies demonstrate promising results concerning the safety and efficacy of long-term stimulation in the primary visual cortex, either via surface electrodes (Niketeghad et al., 2020; Beauchamp et al., 2020) or with intracortical electrodes (Bak et al., 1990; Schmidt et al., 1996; Fernández et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple recent studies.

claim: Stimulation in V1 with intracortical electrodes is estimated to activate tens to thousands of neurons.
source: Stimulation in V1 with intracortical electrodes is estimated to activate tens to thousands of neurons (Histed et al., 2009), resulting in the perception of often 'featureless' white dots of light with a circular shape (Brindley and Lewin, 1968; Bak et al., 1990; Schmidt et al., 1996; Niketeghad et al., 2020; Fernández et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Histed et al., 2009.

claim: Intracortical stimulation in V1 results in the perception of often 'featureless' white dots of light with a circular shape.
source: Stimulation in V1 with intracortical electrodes is estimated to activate tens to thousands of neurons (Histed et al., 2009), resulting in the perception of often 'featureless' white dots of light with a circular shape (Brindley and Lewin, 1968; Bak et al., 1990; Schmidt et al., 1996; Niketeghad et al., 2020; Fernández et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to clinical studies.

claim: Due to cortical magnification, the size of the phosphene increases with its eccentricity.
source: Due to the cortical magnification (the foveal information is represented by a relatively large surface area in the visual cortex as a result of variation of retinal RF size) the size of the phosphene increases with its eccentricity (Winawer and Parvizi, 2016; Bosking et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Winawer and Parvizi, 2016; Bosking et al., 2017.

claim: Phosphene size, stimulation threshold, and brightness depend on stimulation parameters such as pulse width, train length, amplitude, and frequency of stimulation.
source: Furthermore, phosphene size, stimulation threshold (defined as the minimum current to produce a visible phosphene 50% of the time) and brightness depend on stimulation parameters such as the pulse width, train length, amplitude, and frequency of stimulation (Bak et al., 1990; Schmidt et al., 1996; Winawer and Parvizi, 2016; Bosking et al., 2017; Niketeghad et al., 2020; Fernández et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to clinical studies.

claim: The simulator integrates a wide range of clinical results with neurophysiological evidence in humans and non-human primates.
source: The simulator integrates a wide range of clinical results with neurophysiological evidence in humans and non-human primates.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the simulator's design.

claim: The pipeline includes a model of the retinotopic organization and cortical magnification of the visual cortex.
source: The pipeline includes a model of the retinotopic organization and cortical magnification of the visual cortex.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the simulator's components.

claim: The quantitative effects of stimulation parameters and temporal dynamics on phosphene characteristics are incorporated in the simulator.
source: Moreover, the quantitative effects of stimulation parameters and temporal dynamics on phosphene characteristics are incorporated.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the simulator's features.

claim: The simulator is suitable for both computational applications such as end-to-end deep learning-based prosthetic vision optimization as well as behavioral experiments.
source: Our results demonstrate the simulator's suitability for both computational applications such as end-to-end deep learning-based prosthetic vision optimization as well as behavioral experiments.
evidence: The claim is supported by the results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The simulator is implemented in Python using the PyTorch deep learning library.
source: Our simulator is implemented in Python, using the PyTorch deep learning library (Paszke et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the implementation with a citation.

claim: The simulator makes use of differentiable functions which calculate the brightness of each pixel in the output image in parallel.
source: The simulator makes use of differentiable functions which, given the entire set of phosphenes and their modeled properties, calculate the brightness of each pixel in the output image in parallel.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the simulator's architecture.

claim: The simulator uses the reverse wedge-dipole visuotopic model of V1 proposed by Polimeni et al., 2006 for mapping phosphene locations from cortical electrode locations to the visual field.
source: For mapping phosphene locations from the cortical electrode locations to the neuroprosthesis user's visual field, our simulator uses the reverse wedge-dipole visuotopic model of V1, proposed by Polimeni et al., 2006.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Polimeni et al., 2006.

claim: The model accurately fits the reported effect of pulse width, frequency and train duration on the probability of phosphenes perception.
source: The model accurately fits the reported effect of pulse width, frequency and train duration on the probability of phosphenes perception.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison with data from Fernández et al., 2021 shown in Figure 3.

claim: The lowest measured frame rate (10,000 phosphenes at a resolution of 256 × 256) was 28.7 frames per second on an NVIDIA A30 GPU.
source: The lowest measured frame rate (10.000 phosphenes at a resolution of 256 × 256) was 28.7 frames per second.
evidence: The claim is supported by performance testing data presented in Figure 5.

claim: On a consumer-grade GPU (GeForce GTX 1080), the simulator reaches real-time processing speeds (>100 fps) for simulations with 1000 phosphenes at 256 × 256 resolution.
source: Notably, even on a consumer-grade GPU (e.g. a 2016 model GeForce GTX 1080) the simulator still reaches real-time processing speeds (>100 fps) for simulations with 1000 phosphenes at 256 × 256 resolution.
evidence: The claim is supported by performance testing data.

claim: The simulator can run in real-time.
source: We present a biologically plausible, PyTorch-based phosphene simulator that can run in real-time and uses differentiable operations to allow for gradient-based computational optimization of phosphene encoding models.
evidence: The claim is supported by performance data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The simulator uses differentiable operations to allow for gradient-based computational optimization of phosphene encoding models.
source: We present a biologically plausible, PyTorch-based phosphene simulator that can run in real-time and uses differentiable operations to allow for gradient-based computational optimization of phosphene encoding models.
evidence: The claim is supported by the implementation details and demonstration in end-to-end optimization experiments.

claim: The modular and open-source software provides a flexible simulation framework for computational, clinical, and behavioral neuroscientists working on visual neuroprosthetics.
source: The modular and open-source software provides a flexible simulation framework for computational, clinical, and behavioral neuroscientists working on visual neuroprosthetics.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the software's design and availability.

claim: The brightness and detection threshold of each phosphene are based on a model of the intracortical tissue activation in response to electrical stimulation with biphasic square pulse trains.
source: The brightness and detection threshold of each phosphene are based on a model of the intracortical tissue activation in response to electrical stimulation with biphasic square pulse trains.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the model's basis.

claim: The model assumes brightness and detection thresholds of phosphene perception to be primarily correlated with the deposited charge.
source: The model assumes brightness and detection thresholds of phosphene perception to be primarily correlated with the deposited charge, and accounts for the relative inefficiency of higher stimulation frequencies, longer pulse widths, and longer train durations, as found in Winawer and Parvizi, 2016; Niketeghad et al., 2020; Fernández et al., 2021.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to relevant studies.

claim: The simulator accounts for basic accommodation effects on brightness for prolonged or repeated stimulation using a memory trace of the stimulation history.
source: Using a memory trace of the stimulation history, the simulator accounts for basic accommodation effects on brightness for prolonged or repeated stimulation, as described in prior work (Schmidt et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Schmidt et al., 1996.

claim: The model accounts for experimental data on the accommodation in response to repeated stimulation in time periods up to 200 s.
source: The results presented in Figure 4 reveal that the model accounts for experimental data on the accommodation in response to repeated stimulation in time periods up to 200 s.
evidence: The claim is supported by data comparison shown in Figure 4.

claim: The simulator predicts a moderate recovery over the next 1000s, in contrast to the findings by Schmidt et al., 1996.
source: However, in contrast to the findings by Schmidt et al., 1996, our simulator predicts a moderate recovery over the next 1000s.
evidence: The claim is based on model predictions compared to experimental data.

claim: The modeled recovery largely stays within the 95% confidence interval of the experimental data.
source: Although we cannot provide an explanation for this difference, the modeled recovery largely stays within the 95% confidence interval of the experimental data.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison with experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The simulator is the first to incorporate empirical models of the current spread in cortical tissue to simulate the effects of stimulation current on the phosphene size.
source: However, our simulator is the first to incorporate empirical models of the current spread in cortical tissue (Tehovnik and Slocum, 2007; Winawer and Parvizi, 2016; Bosking et al., 2017) to simulate the effects of stimulation current on the phosphene size.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison with previous work and citations to the models used.

claim: The simulator can be tailored to simulate custom alternative scenarios including different phosphene shapes.
source: Although the simulator, by default, assumes round phosphene percepts that are independently activated, it can be tailored to simulate custom alternative scenarios: the phosphene maps can be adjusted to simulate different shapes (see Figure 1—figure supplement 2), and it is possible to simulate arbitrary interactions between electrodes with minor adaptations to our code (see Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by description and demonstration in supplementary figures.

claim: The modular design of the simulator allows for future extensions to simulate brain stimulation in other regions such as lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN) or higher visual areas.
source: The modular design of the simulator allows for future extensions to simulate brain stimulation in other regions such as lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN) or higher visual areas (Murphey and Maunsell, 2007; Pezaris and Reid, 2007; Panetsos et al., 2011; Mirochnik and Pezaris, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to relevant studies and the modular design.

claim: The simulator was initialized with 1000 possible phosphenes in both hemifields, covering a field of view of 16° of visual angle in the dynamic end-to-end encoding experiment.
source: The simulator is initialized with 1000 possible phosphenes in both hemifields, covering a field of view of 16° of visual angle.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the experimental setup.

claim: The model successfully learned to represent the original input frames in phosphene vision over time after training for 45 epochs.
source: We can observe that the model has successfully learned to represent the original input frames in phosphene vision over time, and the decoder is able to approximately reconstruct the original input.
evidence: The claim is supported by the results shown in Figure 7.

claim: In the free optimization condition, the encoder encoded brighter areas of the input picture with large stimulation amplitudes (over 2000 µA).
source: Importantly, the encoder encoded brighter areas of the input picture with large stimulation amplitudes (over 2000 µA).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the model's learned encoding strategy.

claim: The encoding strategy found in the unconstrained optimization scheme is not feasible for real-life applications.
source: The encoding strategy found in such an unconstrained optimization scheme is not feasible for real-life applications.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on knowledge of practical constraints in neuroprosthetics.

claim: In the constrained condition, the encoder was reconfigured to output 10 discrete values between 0 and 128 µA.
source: To evaluate whether our end-to-end pipeline can be harnessed to optimize the encoding in a constrained context, we performed a second training run (the constrained condition) where we reconfigured the encoder to output 10 discrete values between 0 and 128 µA.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the experimental setup.

claim: The decoder is able to accurately reconstruct the original input in the safety-constrained training condition.
source: Nevertheless, the decoder is able to accurately reconstruct the original input.
evidence: The claim is supported by the results shown in Figure 8.

claim: In the supervised boundary condition, the model successfully converged to a sparse phosphene encoding that selectively represents the object boundaries.
source: Note that the model successfully converged to a sparse phosphene encoding that selectively represents the object boundaries.
evidence: The claim is supported by the results shown in Figure 8.

claim: Adding a coactivation current resulted in a significant increase of simultaneously active neighboring electrodes (p < 0.001).
source: Adding a coactivation current resulted in a significant increase of simultaneously active neighboring electrodes. (p < 0.001 for both comparisons with the baseline condition).
evidence: The claim is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 4.

claim: The simulator is well-suited for the dynamic optimization in an end-to-end architecture.
source: The results presented in Figure 7 demonstrate that our proposed realistic phosphene simulator is well-suited for the dynamic optimization in an end-to-end architecture.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental results shown in Figure 7.

claim: The proof-of-principle video-encoding experiments are the first to explicitly optimize the stimulation across the temporal domain.
source: Our proof-of-principle video-encoding experiments are the first to explicitly optimize the stimulation across the temporal domain.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison with previous work in the field.

claim: The simulator is well-suited for the optimization of prosthetic vision to natural stimuli and can be configured to comply with constraints of the stimulation protocol.
source: The results presented in Figure 8 demonstrate that our simulator is well-suited for the optimization of prosthetic vision to natural stimuli and that it can be configured to comply with constraints of the stimulation protocol.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental results shown in Figure 8.

claim: The quality of the reconstructions for the constrained version of the encoder indicate that the model can still find an efficient information encoding strategy using a limited set of stimulation amplitudes.
source: Note that the quality of the reconstructions for the constrained version of the encoder indicate that the model can still find an efficient information encoding strategy using a limited set of stimulation amplitudes (10 discrete values between 0 and 128 μA).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the reconstruction quality shown in Figure 8.

claim: A realistic and biologically-plausible simulator has been developed for retinal prosthetic vision (Pulse2Percept).
source: Meanwhile, a realistic and biologically-plausible simulator has been developed for retinal prosthetic vision (Pulse2Percept, Beyeler et al., 2017), which takes into account the axonal spread of activation along ganglion cells and temporal nonlinearities to construct plausible simulations of stimulation patterns.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Beyeler et al., 2017.

claim: A biophysically-grounded simulation model for the functional evaluation of cortical prosthetic vision remains to be developed.
source: Even though scientists increasingly realize that more realistic models of phosphene vision are required to narrow the gap between simulations and reality (Han et al., 2021; Dagnelie, 2008), a biophysically-grounded simulation model for the functional evaluation of cortical prosthetic vision remains to be developed.
evidence: The claim is based on a review of the literature and identification of a gap.

claim: The source code of the simulator can be retrieved from GitHub.
source: The source code of our simulator can be retrieved from GitHub (copy archived at de Ruyter van Steveninck, 2024a).
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about code availability.

claim: The latest stable release can be installed using pip: $ pip install dynaphos.
source:
The latest stable release can be installed using pip:

$ pip install dynaphos.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about software installation.

claim: The simulator provides the option of substituting the visuotopic mapping equations with other estimates such as the mono- or dipole model in Polimeni et al., 2006; Schwartz, 1983.
source: Note that in our simulation software, we provide the option of substituting Equations 1, 2, 3 and 4, with other estimates described such as the mono- or dipole model in Polimeni et al., 2006; Schwartz, 1983.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the software's flexibility with citations.

claim: The framework is compatible with the retinotopic maps of other structures, such as the LGN.
source: We note, however, that the framework is compatible with the retinotopic maps of other structures, such as the LGN, which is the structure providing input to the primary visual cortex.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the framework's compatibility.

claim: The simulation software provides the option to substitute the current spread equation with an estimate by Bosking et al., 2017.
source: In our simulation software, we provide the option to substitute Equation 6 with an estimate by Bosking et al., 2017.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the software's flexibility with a citation.

claim: The simulator uses a thresholding model based on psychometric data from Fernández et al., 2021.
source: Our simulator uses a thresholding model based on psychometric data from Fernández et al., 2021.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to the data source.

claim: By default, the detection thresholds remain constant after initialization.
source: Note that, by default, the detection thresholds remain constant after initialization.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the default model behavior.

claim: The memory trace is used for the phosphene brightness and not the phosphene size.
source: Note that the memory trace is used for the phosphene brightness and not the phosphene size.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the model's design.

claim: Only the instantaneous current is used in the calculation of the phosphene size because there is little experimental data on the temporal dynamics of phosphene size in relation to the accumulated charge.
source: Because there is little experimental data on the temporal dynamics of phosphene size in relation to the accumulated charge, only the instantaneous current is used in the calculation of the phosphene size.
evidence: The claim is based on the lack of experimental data and a modeling decision.

claim: Some studies have found accommodation over different time scales and sometimes no accommodation at all, in contrast to Schmidt et al., 1996.
source: In contrast to the findings by Schmidt et al., 1996, some studies have found accommodation over different time scales and sometimes no accommodation at all (Bak et al., 1990; Fernández et al., 2021; Bartlett et al., 1977; Dobelle and Mladejovsky, 1974).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies showing variability.

claim: More research is required for a better understanding of the neural response after repeated or prolonged stimulation.
source: More research is required for a better understanding of the neural response after repeated or prolonged stimulation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the ambivalence in clinical data.

claim: More elongated shapes and more complex shapes have been reported for phosphenes in addition to round shapes.
source: However, more elongated shapes and more complex shapes have been reported as well (Bosking et al., 2017; Winawer and Parvizi, 2016; Bak et al., 1990).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to clinical reports.

claim: The simulator enables easy adjustments of the appearance of individual phosphenes by using separately generated phosphene renderings.
source: By using separately generated phosphene renderings, our simulator enables easy adjustments of the appearance of individual phosphenes.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the simulator's design.

claim: The simulator incorporated the possibility to change the default Gaussian blob appearance into Gabor patches with a specific frequency and orientation.
source: Additionally, we incorporated the possibility to change the default Gaussian blob appearance into Gabor patches with a specific frequency and orientation.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the simulator's features.

claim: There is ambivalence in the reports regarding phosphene color, including descriptions ranging from black or white to different tones of color.
source: Regarding the color of phosphenes, there is still some ambivalence in the reports, including descriptions of phosphene color ranging from black or white to different tones of color (Tehovnik and Slocum, 2007; Tehovnik et al., 2009; Schmidt et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies showing variability.

claim: Increasing the stimulation amplitudes can lead the phosphene appearance to shift from colored to yellowish or white.
source: Notably, increasing the stimulation amplitudes can lead the appearance to shift from colored to yellowish or white (Schmidt et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Schmidt et al., 1996.

claim: The shift in phosphene appearance with higher stimulation amplitudes may be explained by the increased current spread spanning multiple cortical columns coding for different visual characteristics.
source: This effect may be explained by the increased current spread for higher stimulation amplitudes, which is predicted to span multiple cortical columns coding for different visual characteristics (e.g. orientation or color), thus giving rise to phosphenes with amalgamated features (Tehovnik and Slocum, 2007).
evidence: The claim is based on a theoretical explanation with a citation.

claim: The limited amount of systematic data render it difficult to enable more accurate simulations of the variability in phosphene appearance.
source: Currently, the limited amount of systematic data render it difficult to enable more accurate simulations of the variability in phosphene appearance.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the state of available data.

claim: Dynamic optimization of the stimulation may be necessary to counteract unwanted effects such as response fading due to accommodation after repeated or prolonged stimulation.
source: Dynamic optimization of the stimulation may be necessary to counteract unwanted effects such as response fading due to accommodation after repeated or prolonged stimulation (Schmidt et al., 1996), or delayed phosphene perception after stimulation on- and offset.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from known effects with a citation.

claim: The inclusion of a realistic simulator in the optimization pipeline enables researchers to exploit the optimal combination of stimulation parameters to obtain precise control over the required perception.
source: The inclusion of a realistic simulator in the optimization pipeline enables researchers to exploit the optimal combination of stimulation parameters to obtain precise control over the required perception.
evidence: The claim is an inference about the benefits of the simulator.

claim: Dynamic phosphene encoding could prove useful to expand the encoded information along the temporal domain.
source: Moreover, besides acquiring optimal control over the transfer function from stimulation to phosphenes, dynamic phosphene encoding could also prove useful to expand the encoded information along the temporal domain (Beauchamp et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is speculative with a supporting citation.

claim: The software is well-suited for simulation experiments that further investigate dynamic stimulation.
source: Although this was not in the scope of the current study, our software is well-suited for simulation experiments that further investigate dynamic stimulation.
evidence: The claim is an inference about the software's capabilities.

claim: There remain some challenging perceptual considerations for the design of useful dynamical stimulation patterns.
source: Note that there remain some challenging perceptual considerations for the design of useful dynamical stimulation patterns (for an excellent review on asynchronous stimulation in relation to flicker fusion, form vision, and apparent motion perception, please see Moleirinho et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a review.

claim: The results are in line with previous results on constrained end-to-end optimization, indicating that task-relevant information can be maximized under sparsity constraints.
source: These results are in line with previous results on constrained end-to-end optimization, indicating that task-relevant information can be maximized under sparsity constraints (de Ruyter van Steveninck et al., 2022a).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison with previous work and a citation.

claim: A visual prosthesis may need to prioritize task-relevant information, rather than providing an accurate description of the visual surroundings.
source: Ultimately, a visual prosthesis may need to prioritize task-relevant information, rather than providing an accurate description of the visual surroundings.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on practical considerations.

claim: In recent SPV research with sighted human observers, much attention is devoted to semantic (boundary) segmentation for discriminating the important information from irrelevant background.
source: For this reason, in recent SPV research with sighted human observers much attention is devoted to semantic (boundary) segmentation for discriminating the important information from irrelevant background (Sanchez-Garcia et al., 2020; Han et al., 2021; Rasla and Beyeler, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: The explored image processing strategies in behavioral studies are equally compatible with the automated optimization through an end-to-end machine learning pipeline.
source: Note that the explored image processing strategies in these behavioral studies are equally compatible with the automated optimization through an end-to-end machine learning pipeline.
evidence: The claim is an inference about the compatibility of approaches.

claim: Computational optimization approaches can aid in the development of safe stimulation protocols by allowing faster exploration of the large parameter space.
source: Computational optimization approaches can also aid in the development of safe stimulation protocols, because they allow a faster exploration of the large parameter space and enable task-driven optimization of image processing strategies (Granley et al., 2022a; Fauvel and Chalk, 2022; White et al., 2019; Küçükoğlu et al., 2022; de Ruyter van Steveninck et al., 2022a; Ghaffari et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The development of task-relevant scene-processing algorithms will likely benefit both from computational optimization experiments as well as exploratory SPV studies with human observers.
source: Ultimately, the development of task-relevant scene-processing algorithms will likely benefit both from computational optimization experiments as well as exploratory SPV studies with human observers.
evidence: The claim is an inference about future research directions.

claim: The encoder learns to make use of the leak current in the electrode coactivation condition.
source: The electrode coactivation resulted in a higher percentage of active neighboring electrodes compared to the baseline, suggesting that the encoder learns to make use of the leak current.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the experimental results shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 4.

claim: It is important to consider the subjective interpretability of the simulated phosphene representation besides the encoding efficiency.
source: Besides the encoding efficiency (characterized by the computational decodability of task-relevant information), it is important to consider the subjective interpretablitity of the simulated phosphene representation.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on practical considerations.

claim: The model has successfully learned to preserve correspondences between the phosphene representation and the input image in all of the training conditions.
source: In Figure 8 it can be observed that the model has successfully learned to preserve correspondences between the phosphene representation and the input image in all of the training conditions.
evidence: The claim is supported by visual inspection of Figure 8.

claim: The preservation of subjective interpretability in an automated optimization pipeline remains a non-trivial challenge, especially when using natural stimuli.
source: The preservation of subjective interpretability in an automated optimization pipeline remains a non-trivial challenge, especially when using natural stimuli.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the complexity of the problem.

claim: The distinct punctate phosphenes are in nature very dissimilar from natural images, possibly hampering perceptual similarity metrics that rely on low-level feature correspondence.
source: This may be even more important for cortical prostheses, as the distinct punctate phosphenes are in nature very dissimilar from natural images, possibly hampering perceptual similarity metrics that rely on low-level feature correspondence.
evidence: The claim is an inference about the challenges specific to cortical prostheses.

claim: The functional quality of the artificial vision will depend on both the correspondence between the visual environment and the phosphene encoding, and the implant recipient's ability to extract that information into a usable percept.
source: Eventually, the functional quality of the artificial vision will not only depend on the correspondence between the visual environment and the phosphene encoding, but also on the implant recipient's ability to extract that information into a usable percept.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on understanding of perceptual processes.

claim: It will always be important to include human observers (both sighted experimental subjects and actual prosthetic implant users) in the optimization cycle to ensure subjective interpretability for the end user.
source: Regardless of the implementation, it will always be important to include human observers (both sighted experimental subjects and actual prosthetic implant users) in the optimization cycle to ensure subjective interpretability for the end user (Fauvel and Chalk, 2022; Beyeler and Sanchez-Garcia, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations and represents a methodological recommendation.

claim: The model runs in real-time and is faster than the state-of-the-art realistic simulation for retinal prostheses.
source: Although our model runs in real-time and is faster than the state-of-the art realistic simulation for retinal prostheses (Beyeler et al., 2017), there is a trade-off between speed and the memory demand.
evidence: The claim is supported by performance data and comparison with cited work.

claim: There is a trade-off between speed and memory demand in the simulator.
source: Although our model runs in real-time and is faster than the state-of-the art realistic simulation for retinal prostheses (Beyeler et al., 2017), there is a trade-off between speed and the memory demand.
evidence: The claim is based on the architecture of the simulator.

claim: Several simulators exist for cortical prostheses that run in real-time without requiring a dedicated graphics card.
source: While several simulators exist for cortical prostheses that run in real-time without requiring a dedicated graphics card (Li, 2013; Wong et al., 2010), none of these incorporate current spread-based models of phosphene size, realistic stimulation parameter ranges or temporal dynamics.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to existing simulators.

claim: None of the existing real-time simulators for cortical prostheses incorporate current spread-based models of phosphene size, realistic stimulation parameter ranges or temporal dynamics.
source: While several simulators exist for cortical prostheses that run in real-time without requiring a dedicated graphics card (Li, 2013; Wong et al., 2010), none of these incorporate current spread-based models of phosphene size, realistic stimulation parameter ranges or temporal dynamics.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison with existing work cited.

claim: A convenient direction would be the implementation of the simulator using the Cg shader programming language for graphics processing, which is used in 3D game engines like Unreal Engine, or Unity 3D.
source: More specifically, a convenient direction would be the implementation of our simulator using the Cg shader programming language for graphics processing, which is used in 3D game engines like Unreal Engine, or Unity 3D, as previously demonstrated for epiretinal simulations by Thorn et al., 2020.
evidence: The claim is a suggestion for future work with a citation to a precedent.

claim: Even after loss of vision, the brain integrates eye movements for the localization of visual stimuli.
source: Even after loss of vision, the brain integrates eye movements for the localization of visual stimuli (Reuschel et al., 2012), and in cortical prostheses the position of the artificially induced percept will shift along with eye movements (Brindley and Lewin, 1968; Schmidt et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to relevant studies.

claim: In cortical prostheses, the position of the artificially induced percept will shift along with eye movements.
source: Even after loss of vision, the brain integrates eye movements for the localization of visual stimuli (Reuschel et al., 2012), and in cortical prostheses the position of the artificially induced percept will shift along with eye movements (Brindley and Lewin, 1968; Schmidt et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to clinical observations.
